spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the module-map contract that matters in practice — same specifier returns the cached module, a query-string specifier is a genuinely new module — using the real import-with-type surface and an honest fetch fallback.

interactive.rationale: Editable JSON textarea with live re-render, Render, re-import and cache-bust buttons, a facts grid, and the imported template shown verbatim.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises a rendered editable template plus what the module cache does and does not do, which is exactly the page.

edge_cases.rationale: Invalid JSON produces a labelled in-place error (verified), the fetch fallback rethrows non-TypeError failures and checks response.ok, and the unsupported branch renarrates each button honestly.

conformance.rationale: The suite's text-import-is-cached-by-specifier assertion is the exact contract the reload buttons teach.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: initial render produced the full receipt from the fetched 95-char template; editing the JSON re-rendered (Espresso substitution verified); '{bad json' showed the labelled parse error; re-import and cache-bust both ran with fetch-path narration since text modules are unsupported here; console clean apart from the expected aborted probe import; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Reimports log and emit showcaseTelemetry.assert('template-reimported', …) with the path taken and call count.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, secondary buttons override background and color, monospace editing surface, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: The textarea is labelled, outputs are focusable pre blocks, the facts grid uses dl semantics, and status messages land in an aria-live output.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; the split grid stacks on mobile with a usable textarea.

openQuestions.title: Rename the 'import calls' fact on the fetch path
openQuestions.detail: loadTemplate() increments the counter shown as 'import calls' even when the browser has no text modules and every call is a fetch — on this browser the grid reads 'import calls: 1' for what the banner just said was a fetch. Label it 'loads' or switch the label by path so the facts and the banner cannot disagree.

openQuestions.title: Cache-vs-disk staleness claim needs a Chrome 155 verification pass
openQuestions.detail: The re-import narration ('if you edited the file on disk you would still be looking at the old text') and the module-map timings are only exercisable on a text-modules browser; Chromium 141 cannot reach that branch. Verify once on 155/Canary that re-import serves the cached module with ~0ms and the ?v= specifier actually refetches.

summary: A real practical shape with the right cache lesson attached. Verified over CDP on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) at http://localhost:3000/v155/import-text-text-modules/template-runner/: initial render, live JSON editing, the invalid-JSON error state, re-import and cache-bust all behaved with honest fetch-path narration since text modules are unsupported here; console and network clean apart from the intended probe abort; no overflow on either class. Feature /conformance/ route ran 3 pass / 3 fail (honest pre-155 gaps). Two minor label/verification nits recorded.
